2018_122_060518regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of June 5, 2018, held at 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R. The meeting is almost entirely a student-recognition night: 59 lettered recognition items from A through GGG cover the synchronized swim state champions, all-state winter athletes, senior scholar athletes and dozens of academic, arts and robotics competitions. The only action items sit on the consent agenda — minutes of the May 1 workshop and May 15 meeting, and a resolution setting a public hearing on the proposed 2018-2019 budget for June 19, 2018 at the Services Building.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, June 5, 2018, 7:00 P.M., Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (items A through GGG, followed by a five-minute recess); Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Adjournment. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker, with the President able to shorten the limit to accommodate everyone. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
Mike Jolly reads the three athletics items; the remaining scripts are assigned to board members by first name (Karl, Steve, Gary, Paula, Elizabeth, Todd, Nancy). Items 2.A through 2.C name the Synchronized Swim State Champions by grade and school, the All-State Athletes for Winter 2017, and the Senior Scholar Athletes for 2017-2018 who carried a 3.5 grade point average. Items 2.D through 2.GGG recognize competition results, among them: AMC8 first and second in the nation (Boulan Park); a 2nd in Nation at the Intermediate Level in the 13th Annual Chinese Bridge Speech Contest at the University of Massachusetts; "Best in Show" at the 50th Michigan Student Film Festival at the DIA's Detroit Film Theatre for a Larson documentary on the Bosnian War, with Athens taking Best of Show for "Don't Turn Your Windshield Into A Screen," "Saving Lake St. Clair" and "Athens Fringe Fest"; an IA-East FIRST Robotics team placing 30th in the Curie Division at the World Championships, with a student named to the First Deans List, one of ten students in the world; MATHCOUNTS 1st in State and 7th and 12th in Nation; a 2nd place internationally at the Intel Science and Engineering Fair for "Context-Aware Medical Image Super-Resolution using Convolutional Neural Networks"; a Michigan History Day national finalist website, "The Internment of Japanese Americans"; 1st place in the U.S. in the National High School Biology Scholarship; and 1st in Nation at the Washington University Chemistry Tournament against 54 other teams.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
A. Minutes of the May 1, 2018 Board Workshop. B. Minutes of the May 15, 2018 Board Meeting. C. Resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2018/2019 school year budget.

**May 15, 2018 minutes, as attached**
The May meeting recognized the Facilities Study Attendance Area Review Team — City Attorney Lori Bluhm, Emily Cremers, Pupil Accounting Coordinator Laura Duzey, Jeff Frederick, Victoria King, Veronica Pala, Delia Rodi-Barczys, Lori Sisk and Courtney Spangler, with Mark Dziatczak and Kris Griffor as administrative liaisons — and named Tina Houser, Health Care Aide at Morse Elementary, the Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year from seventeen nominees. The retiree list runs to twenty-eight names, described by the superintendent as 688 years of collective service.

Nine administrative appointments passed, each a two-year probationary contract without tenure: Kandice Moynihan as Finance Director (June 6, 2018), John Pagel as Director of Employee Services, Tim Fulcher as Director of Athletics, Continuing Education and Enrichment, Sarah Young as Special Education Supervisor, Erin Keyser as Director of Early Childhood Programs, Shari Pawlus as Principal of Hill Elementary, Jonathan Cross as Principal of Baker Middle School, Anthony Morse as Principal of Boulan Park Middle School and Christian Mueller as Principal of Smith Middle School, the last eight effective July 1, 2018. Business actions awarded flooring replacement to Conventional Carpet at $650,000.00 and asbestos abatement to Abatement & Demolition Services at $37,645.00, both from the Building Site and Sinking Project Fund. Under Public Act 419 of 2004 the Board designated Mr. Steve Gottlieb as its representative to the 2018 Oakland Schools electoral body and directed him to vote for Dr. Theresa Rich and Mr. Marc Katz for six-year terms ending June 30, 2024. Every vote recorded 6 yes, 0 no, with Philippart absent.

**5.C. Budget public hearing**
Michigan law requires a public hearing on a proposed budget with notice at least six days ahead, stating the time and place, where the proposed budget may be inspected, and — in 11-point bold faced type — that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied will be a subject of the hearing. The resolution sets the hearing for June 19, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, and makes copies available at the Administration Building from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., June 13 through June 19, 2018. Exhibit A carries the notice text for publication.

**Recognition — academic and arts competitions.** 2.D American Mathematics Contest (AMC8), Boulan Park Middle School: two students placed 1st and 2nd nationally. 2.E American Scholastic League, Boulan Park: two State Champions. 2.F Chinese Bridge Speech Contest, Troy High: the 13th Annual contest, a half-day event held March 31st in Boston at the University of Massachusetts, open to students without Chinese heritage; a Troy High student is a National Semifinalist. 2.P HOSA, IA-East and Troy High: IA-East placed 1st in State in Dental Terminology, Community Emergency Response Team Skills and KT Pathophysiology, advancing to Nationals in June; Troy High students at the 2018 HOSA Leadership Conference placed 1st in State in "Prepared Speaking," "Epidemiology," "Medical Innovation (Existing)" and "Biomedical Laboratory Science." 2.Q Intel Science and Engineering Fair, Troy High: over 1,800 students from over 80 countries competed; the students' work, Context-Aware Medical Image Super-Resolution using Convolutional Neural Networks, was awarded second place by the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence, and they placed 2nd internationally. 2.R Japanese Quiz Bowl, Athens: held at Eastern Michigan University and sponsored by the Japanese Teachers Association of Michigan; Athens students placed 1st in State in Level 4. 2.S MATHCOUNTS, Boulan Park: 1st in State, 7th and 12th in Nation. 2.T Michigan Brain Bee, Athens: 1st in State. 2.U Michigan China Quiz Bowl, Troy High: 1st in State in their division. 2.V Michigan Council for Economic Education, Troy High: State Champ team for both the AP and 1B Division and the non-AP Division. 2.W Michigan History Day, Boulan Park and Larson: Boulan Park placed 1st in State and will compete as National Finalists at the University of Maryland in June for the group website "The Internment of Japanese Americans"; Larson students placed 1st in State for a musical about the Declaration of Sentiments, winning "Best Use of Music/Arts" in the junior division at the state competition in Bay City and advancing to nationals in Washington, D.C. 2.X MITES State Competition, Athens: the society was established in 1928; Athens students received 1st in State for their Multiple Piece 3D Print Group Project and for CAD Rapid Prototyping Models Assembly. 2.Y MIPA Journalism, Athens and Troy High: the association was founded in 1912; Athens took 1st in State in Sports Feature for "Reinventing JVB," Music Video for "See the Sun" and Short Film for "Cold Medicine," while Troy High won "All-State Journalism Staff" and "All-MIPA Yearbook Winner," the Gladiator Yearbook Staff won the "Spartan Award with Distinction" and the Chariot Newspaper Staff the "Gold Medal with Distinction." 2.Z Michigan Japanese Speech Contest, Athens: sponsored by the General Consulate of Detroit and the Japanese Business Society of Detroit; one student won 1st in State and another won the Consulate General's Award. 2.AA Michigan Junior Chess Championship, IA-East: 1st in State in the Junior (K-12) championships, representing Michigan at the 2018 Denker Tournament of High School Champions in Wisconsin, with only one student chosen per state. 2.BB Michigan Mathematics League, Boulan Park: 1st in State in the individual division and as a team. 2.CC MSBOA District State Solo and Ensemble, Athens: 1st in State, 1st Division. 2.DD MSBOA Michigan All-State Middle School Band, Boulan Park: an average of over 2,000 students audition each year for the 400 seats across five ensembles in 10-minute recorded auditions; Boulan Park students received 1st in State for Trombone, French Horn and Trumpet. 2.EE MSBOA All-State Middle School Orchestra, Boulan Park and Smith: students placed 1st in State. 2.FF MSVMA State Solo and Ensemble, Athens: a First Division rating. 2.GG NATAS Michigan Student Production Awards, Athens: wins for Best Video Essay ("Reinventing JVB"), Best Music Video ("See The Sun"), Best Animation ("Don't Turn Your Windshield Into A Screen"), Best Public Affairs ("Detroit Street Care"), Best Writing ("Cold Medicine"), Best Public Service Announcement ("No Matter What"), Best Director ("Movement"), Best Photographer ("Above & Below") and Best Editing. 2.HH National Economics Challenge, Troy High: each year over 11,000 students across the U.S. participate; 23 Michigan middle school teams participated and Boulan Park's team, "Pulverizing Pancake," tied for 1st in State with Detroit Country Day School. 2.SS Quiz Bowl (America Answers), Boulan Park: a contest of 100 multiple-choice questions; students placed 2nd in Nation. 2.TT Quiz Bowl (Great Lakes), Boulan Park: 1st in State. 2.UU Quiz Bowl (NAQT), Smith: after victories at Detroit Catholic High School and Detroit Country Day, the team finished 1st in State and was invited to compete in Chicago in May. 2.VV Scholastic Art and Writing Awards, Boulan Park, Athens and Troy High: the program was founded in 1923 and serves grades 7-12; students received Gold Key Awards for Art and Drawing. 2.WW Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit, Larson: held annually at Cobo Hall; Larson students won 1st in State for U.S. Navy, Broadcom Masters, U.S. Department of Commerce and Oceans and Atmosphere, and the SEFMD Grand Award. 2.XX Science Olympiad State Competition, Troy High: 23 events with teams of 15 students; Troy High won 1st in State for Anatomy and Physiology, Materials Science, Microbe Mission and Optics. 2.YY Siemens Foundation Math and Science Research Competition, Troy High: established in 1999; students are National Finalists. 2.ZZ Sutton Foster Ovation Musical Theater Award, Troy High: presented at Michigan State University and named for the two-time Tony Award winner and Troy High School graduate; **Consent agenda.** Item 5 asks approval of items A, B and C together: minutes of the May 1, 2018 Board Workshop, minutes of the May 15, 2018 Board Meeting, and a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2018/2019 school year budget.

**Attached minutes, May 1, 2018 workshop.** President Schmidt called the workshop to order at 6:02 p.m. at the Administration Building. Present with him were Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Gottlieb and Mr. Hauff; Mrs. Hammond participated by phone conference at 6:45 p.m.; Mr. Miletti, Dr. Philippart and Superintendent Machesky were absent. Also present were Mr. Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching & Learning, and administrators Carson, Griffor, Harris and West, with one member of the audience. The agenda covered public communication, a Business Services update on sinking fund flooring projects and asbestos abatement, an Employee Services staffing update, and board professional learning on homework. The meeting adjourned at 8:45 p.m. Gary N. Hauff signed as Secretary.

**Attached minutes, May 15, 2018 meeting at Athens High School.** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. Present were Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Miletti; Dr. Philippart was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, Brasington, Duda, Jansen, Griffor, Pagel, Jolly, Cottone, Fulcher, Mills, Pass, Carrier, Morse, Cross, Kwasny, Jagels, Glasser, Harris and West; and approximately 160 members of the audience.

The TSD Mission Moment recognized the Facilities Study Attendance Area Review Team, formed to review attendance area patterns, resolve double split learning pathways, address overcrowding and imbalance across buildings, and minimize changes to attendance areas. Recognized were City Attorney Lori Bluhm, Emily Cremers, TSD Pupil Accounting Coordinator Laura Duzey, Jeff Frederick, Victoria King, Veronica Pala, Delia Rodi-Barczys, Lori Sisk and Courtney Spangler, with Deputy Superintendent for Teaching & Learning Mark Dziatczak and Assistant Superintendent for Elementary Instruction Kris Griffor as administrative liaisons.

Seventeen nominees for the Outstanding Support Staff Award were recognized: Mike Boussie (Safe Ed, Troy College and Career High School), Robert Dean (Custodian, Hamilton Elementary), Jeannette Eve (Tier 1 Program Assistant, Troy Center for Transition), Keith Giacoma (Health Care Aide, Wass Elementary), Karen Hilty (Food Service Supervisor, Smith Middle School), Barb Johnson (Secretary, Athletics), Kathy Koncagul (Computer Tech, Leonard Elementary), Sharon Kreza (Secretary, Wattles Elementary), Garry Marble (Custodian, Wattles Elementary), Nancy Mosey (Paraprofessional, Barnard Elementary), Tony Recchia (Bus Driver, Hamilton Elementary), Majd Tominna (ELD Paraprofessional, Troy High), Meena Trivedi (ELD Paraprofessional, Hamilton Elementary), Nancy Wells (Computer Tech, Athens High), Austin Woodard (Paraprofessional, Boulan Park), Seth Wyatt (Paraprofessional, Costello Elementary) and Tina Houser (Health Care Aide, Morse Elementary). Tina Houser was named Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year and her name was sent to the county for the county-wide award.

The retirees introduced were Anaam Asmar (Para-Professional, Martell, since 1997), Janice Brzezinski (Administrator, Hill, since 1979), Karen Chick (Teacher, Schroeder, since 1989), Kathleen Everlove (GSRP Associate Teacher, Troy Union, since 1999), Rebecca Haga (Childhood Supervisor, Niles Center, since 1986), Karen Hoffman (Teacher, Services Building, since 1990), Linda Jackson (Para-Professional, Baker, since 2000), Michael Jolly (Administrator, Niles Center, since 2004), Beth Ann Jorgensen (Teacher, International Academy East, since 1996), Kathleen Knapp (Teacher, Services Building, since 1999), Teresa Kniseley (Teacher, Elementary Vocal, since 1996), Cindy Kolesar (Teacher, Hamilton, since 1974), Jo Kwasny (Administrator, Boulan Park, since 1998), Nancy Lining (Teacher, Larson, since 1986), Julie Marjamaa (Teacher, Costello, since 1985), Ivonne Mastracci (Secretary, Troy Union, since 1999), Teresa McCormack (Teacher, Smith, since 1999), Audra Melton (Administrator, Baker, since 2009), Trudi Motzenbecker (Teacher, Wattles, since 2000), Kathlyn O'Bryan (Teacher, Troy High, since 2005), Susan Ohlert (Secretary, Central Office, since 1997), Laurie Pickell (Teacher, Martell, since 1985), Betty Prospal (Administrative Assistant, Central Office, since 1995), Karen Rockwell (Cable Services Coordinator, Services Building, since 1986), Claudia Rzekpa (Teacher, Wass/Martell, since 1996), Nancy Schleicher (Teacher, Hamilton, since 1979), Trevor Smith (Teacher, Troy High, since 1991) and Mary Thomas (Teacher, Wattles, since 1997).

Resolution 18-039, moved by Mr. Schmidt and supported by Mrs. Fleming, supported National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 7-11, 2018. Consent agenda 18-040 approved the April 10, 2018 workshop minutes, the April 17, 2018 meeting minutes, the Treasurer's Report for March 2018 and the Oakland Intermediate School District budget. Nine personnel resolutions each issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure: 18-041 Ms. Kandice Moynihan as Finance Director beginning June 6, 2018; 18-042 Mr. John Pagel as Director, Employee Services effective July 1, 2018; 18-043 Mr. Tim Fulcher as Director, Athletics, Continuing Education and Enrichment as of July 1, 2018; 18-044 Ms. Sarah Young as Special Education Supervisor effective July 1, 2018; 18-045 Ms. Erin Keyser as Director, Early Childhood Programs effective July 1, 2018; 18-046 Ms. Shari Pawlus as Principal, Hill Elementary School effective July 1, 2018; 18-047 Mr. Jonathan Cross as Principal, Baker Middle School effective July 1, 2018; 18-048 Mr. Anthony Morse as Principal, Boulan Park Middle School effective July 1, 2018; and 18-049 Mr. Christian Mueller as Principal, Smith Middle School effective July 1, 2018. Business resolution 18-050 awarded the bid for flooring replacement work to Conventional Carpet in the amount of $650,000.00 as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Project Fund, and 18-051 awarded asbestos abatement work to Abatement & Demolition Services in the amount of $37,645.00 from the same fund. Every one of these votes was recorded as Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

Under Other, the Board addressed the Oakland Schools Board of Education biennial election. Reciting Public Act 419 of 2004, which amended election procedures for intermediate school districts that elect board members at a meeting of constituent-district representatives and requires a resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days before the election and considered at not less than one public meeting, the Board designated Mr. Steve Gottlieb as its representative to the 2018 electoral body, supported candidates Dr. Theresa Rich and Mr. Marc Katz for the two positions each for a term of six years ending June 30, 2024, and directed Gottlieb to vote for them at least on the first ballot at the June 4, 2018 election.

Student representatives reported: Ashlee Badia (Athens High) on prom at Andiamos in Warren, the Ford Drive 4UR School event, 11 Athens students recognized as National Merit students, and graduation on June 9th; Anjana Pisupati (International Academy-East) on the junior robotics team placing 30th out of 67 at the World Level competition at Cobo Hall, an IA-East junior receiving the Dean's List honor awarded to only 10 students across the world, graduation on June 8th and finals starting June 14th; and Nadia Shaouni (Troy College & Career High School) on mock job interviews with professionals and a student who signed with Delta College to play basketball, the second student in Athens' history to break the 1,000-point scoring record. Hana Barre (Troy High School) was not in attendance.

In board comments, Mr. Miletti congratulated the retirees and welcomed the nine new administrators; Mrs. Hammond gave a shout out to Mrs. Kolesar and to the Debate & Forensics team's Ted Ed talks; Mrs. Fleming congratulated the retirees and administrators; Mr. Hauff encouraged viewers to attend end-of-year events; Mr. Gottlieb echoed his colleagues. Dr. Machesky thanked the PE teachers for the 2018 Fitness Run despite rain, noted the Troy Robotics team Hammerheads hosting the First Lego League Tournament at Troy High on Saturday, May 19th at 10:30 a.m. with over 500 attendees, and listed graduations: Project Search on June 6th, Athens and Troy High at the O'Rena on June 9th, Troy College & Career High School on June 13th at Troy High, and the International Academy on May 24th at the Detroit Opera House; he thanked the retirees, whose service he described as 688 years collectively, for their commitment to making oneTROY a special place. Mr. Schmidt described a dinner meeting hosted by the Islamic Center for Greater Detroit with Mr. Dziatczak on cultural proficiency, to which educators from Avondale, Rochester Hills and Troy were invited, congratulated the retirees and new administrators, and gave a shout out to Mr. Harris for his work on the interview process. He noted the next Board Meeting at Athens on June 5th for Student Recognition, a Board Workshop on June 12th at the Administration Building, and a Joint Meeting with Troy City Council on June 22nd at 6:00 p.m. The meeting adjourned at 8:23 p.m.

**5.C. Resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2018-2019 school year budget.** The resolution recites that Michigan law requires every local unit of government, including a school district, to hold a public hearing on its proposed budget with notice at least six days before; that the notice must include the time and place of the hearing and where a copy of the proposed budget is available for public inspection; that the notice must include, in 11-point bold faced type, the statement "THE PROPERTY TAX MILLAGE RATE PROPOSED TO BE LEVIED TO SUPPORT THE PROPOSED BUDGET WILL BE A SUBJECT OF THIS HEARING"; and that the hearing must precede final adoption. It resolves that a public hearing be held on June 19, 2018 at a regular Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, to receive testimony and discuss the proposed 2018-2019 budget, and authorizes the Secretary to publish notice in substantially the form of Exhibit A in a newspaper of general circulation at least six days before the hearing. Exhibit A states that copies of the proposed budget will be available for public inspection at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 13, 2018 through Tuesday, June 19, 2018, and is signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education.
